native.summary: Separate magnified thyroid and parathyroid tissue specimens. Static anatomy only.
native.scale_note: 500 micrometres per unit; representative cells and basal lamina enlarged. Separate specimens, not a whole-organ reconstruction. Saved specimen cuts are intentional.

01 Tissue architecture.note: Anatomy-only comparison of colloid-filled follicles with a solid parathyroid cell population; hide the entire schematic signaling layer together.

02 Thyroid tissue.note: Sectioned prominent left follicle: colloid lumen → apical epithelium → basal lamina → local blood. Basal lamina is a follicular layer, not the organ capsule. No layer is hidden within this specimen.

03 Colloid and follicular basal lamina.note: Layer dissection; epithelium, nuclei, vessels and stroma deliberately hidden to expose acellular colloid and basal lamina.

04 Whole follicular nuclei.note: Nuclear dissection: whole saved nuclei exposed by hiding epithelial bodies; no nucleus is cut.

05 Parathyroid architecture.note: Separate solid parathyroid specimen with chief cells, oxyphil cells, adipocytes and its own circulation. Low extracellular Ca²⁺ is the input; chief-cell PTH is the output. There is no colloid inside this specimen.

06 Parathyroid intracellular dissection.note: Cell bodies, covering and vessels hidden to expose whole nuclei, lipid droplets and oxyphil mitochondria.

07 Separate circulation beds.note: Optional vascular dissection: trace each specimen’s own supply, capillary anastomoses and drainage. Cells and stroma are deliberately hidden only in this view. Open ends at specimen cuts do not imply connection between the two samples.

parts.name: Follicular epithelium
parts.description: A single layer of follicular cells separates the colloid lumen from the basal lamina and nearby blood supply. The cells make thyroglobulin, deliver it apically to colloid, then recover and process stored material before releasing T3/T4 toward blood. Polygonal bodies are enlarged, simplified representatives; they do not diagnose thyroid activity.

parts.name: Colloid
parts.description: Acellular, extracellular thyroglobulin-rich content of the follicular lumen. Thyroid hormones are formed and stored while associated with thyroglobulin; cellular uptake and processing precede release to blood. Translucency is a teaching choice.

parts.name: Follicular basal lamina
parts.description: Specialized extracellular support beneath the follicular epithelium, between its basal surface and connective tissue. Distinct from the gland capsule. Authored as complete on all six follicles before the reversible specimen cut; its 2.5 µm modeled thickness is enlarged for teaching.

parts.name: Follicular cell nuclei
parts.description: Nuclei inside the enlarged representative follicular cell bodies. These identify the cellular epithelium surrounding the acellular colloid; they are not cells within the lumen.

parts.name: Intracellular colloid uptake vesicles
parts.description: Enlarged examples of endocytic colloid droplets near the apical region of follicular cells in three representative follicles. They depict uptake for cellular processing, not marginal empty colloid scallops or a route directly from colloid to blood.

parts.name: Parafollicular C cells
parts.description: Distinct calcitonin-secreting cells seated in basal/interfollicular positions, without a colloid-facing surface. Blue is an identification color. The six representative cells illustrate location and release toward local blood, rather than a physiological C-cell abundance.

parts.name: C-cell nuclei
parts.description: Nuclei contained within the separately identified basal/interfollicular C-cell bodies. Their enclosing cells secrete calcitonin; neither the nuclei nor the cells belong within colloid.

parts.name: Thyroid circulation
parts.description: Local supply, six anastomosing perifollicular vascular beds and drainage, authored as one connected circuit. Red-to-blue color indicates a schematic arterial-to-venous transition, not calculated perfusion or oxygen concentration. External specimen-cut ends are deliberate; internal disconnected ends remain unacceptable.

parts.name: Interfollicular connective tissue
parts.description: Supporting tissue between and beneath follicles carries the local circulation. The curved envelope and upper planar face represent a sampled, dissected tissue region; the planar face is an artificial specimen boundary, not a capsule around each follicle.

parts.name: Capsule
parts.description: Sampled fibrous gland covering along the lower thyroid specimen boundary. It is separate from follicular basal lamina; the upper exposed boundary is a deliberate specimen cut. This tissue sample does not reconstruct the whole thyroid organ.

parts.name: Parathyroid capsule
parts.description: Connective-tissue covering of the separate parathyroid sample. It surrounds a solid cellular glandular region, not a colloid-filled follicle. Thickness and transparency are teaching choices; the review remains unaccepted.

parts.name: Parathyroid stroma
parts.description: Connective tissue supporting parathyroid cells and their local vascular passages. Normal parathyroid cells form cords and clusters separated by vascular stroma; this review uses spaced, enlarged representatives rather than a quantitative packing reconstruction.

parts.name: Parathyroid chief cells
parts.description: Predominant parathyroid endocrine cells and the principal PTH source. Falling extracellular ionized Ca²⁺ promotes PTH release into nearby blood. Twenty-two enlarged representative cells retain the prior relative arrangement; their shapes and spacing are simplified teaching choices.

parts.name: Oxyphil cells
parts.description: Larger, mitochondria-rich parathyroid cells, shown here as three enlarged representatives. Mitochondrial abundance helps distinguish them from chief cells. Their endocrine role is not separately simulated; they should not be described as universally inert or incapable of PTH expression.

parts.name: Parathyroid adipocytes
parts.description: Three representative unilocular fat cells within the parathyroid sample. Adipose content varies with age and individual context; this small illustrative set does not establish a normal glandular fat fraction.

parts.name: Parathyroid chief-cell nuclei
parts.description: Nuclei inside the representative chief cells. Cell bodies and nuclei are distinct, separately selectable parts; modeled size and density are not quantitative histology.

parts.name: Oxyphil-cell nuclei
parts.description: Nuclei inside the larger representative oxyphil bodies. Nuclear appearance is simplified; identification also depends on the surrounding mitochondria-rich cytoplasm.

parts.name: Parathyroid adipocyte nuclei
parts.description: Peripheral nuclei in the representative fat cells, displaced toward the cell edge by each large lipid droplet. They remain intracellular; the exposed section is a teaching view.

parts.name: Parathyroid lipid droplets
parts.description: One large storage droplet within each representative unilocular adipocyte. These are intracellular lipid stores, distinct from colloid and hormone signaling symbols.

parts.name: Oxyphil mitochondria
parts.description: A small illustrative set of enlarged mitochondria within oxyphil-cell cytoplasm. It indicates the characteristic mitochondrial enrichment; organelle number, size and arrangement are schematic rather than a quantitative mitochondrial inventory.

parts.name: Parathyroid circulation
parts.description: Connected local supply, central vascular course, three side loops and drainage serving the separate parathyroid sample. Two external specimen ends are deliberate. Red-to-blue colors are schematic; no vessel bridge or duct connects this sample to the thyroid specimen.
